description: A quantizer for equal divisions of the octave: the octave is cut into 1 to 48 equal steps, any step can be switched out of the scale, and an incoming pitch is pulled to the nearest step left in

inputs.text: The pitch to be quantized, at a volt per octave; a polyphonic cable is quantized channel by channel

outputs.text: The quantized pitch at a volt per octave, with as many channels as the input carries

notes: The number between the two arrows is how many equal steps the octave is cut into, from 1 to 48. Click an arrow to change it by one, or hold an arrow down to run through the values.
The column of strips below the number is the scale, lowest step at the bottom. Click a strip to take that step out or put it back, and drag across several to paint a run of them.
In the scale strip a grey strip is a step out of the scale, amber a step in it, and yellow the step being sounded right now.
The arrows, the number and the scale strips are one display rather than separate controls, so none can be clicked for help. The two jacks are the only controls that can.
The division and the scale are both saved with the patch.
menu: Enable all notes — puts every step of the division back into the scale
Disable all notes — takes every step out of the scale, which leaves the quantizer using all of them again, because a scale with nothing in it is ignored rather than obeyed
